subject: Media Literacy
title: Paying for Stories: Checkbook Journalism
description: A quick, practical guide to Paying for Stories: Checkbook Journalism.

hook.text: A tabloid pays a witness $500,000 for an exclusive interview. The witness's story changes to be more dramatic. Coincidence?

buildup.text: Checkbook journalism means paying sources for information or interviews. It's common in tabloid media.

discovery.text: Payment creates incentives to exaggerate, fabricate, or sensationalize. Sources tell the story the buyer wants to hear.

twist.text: Some argue payment is the only way to get certain stories. Others say it corrupts the information at its source.

climax.text: When money changes hands, motivation changes too. Paid sources are performing, not just reporting.

punchline.text: When a source is paid to talk, ask what they're paid to say.

quiz.question: What is the main ethical concern with checkbook journalism?
options: It's too expensive for small outlets
Payment creates incentives for sources to exaggerate or fabricate
